# Skill pack review 01: contradictions, errors and overlaps

Scope: the 69 skills under `skills/sohrab/`. Review date: 2026-10-18. This is the verified and corrected edition of the first draft.
Companion files: `02-optimization.md`, `03-new-skill-proposals.md`. Per-lane verdict notes: `verification/`.

## Method and evidence status

- The first draft (a Haiku 5.5 agent) was re-checked item by item. Six read-only lanes (Sonnet 5.5) re-read the cited passages by content, not by line number alone. The parent re-read these items itself: A11, A12, A33, A34, A43 (the "should not implement" wording), and the item that was removed as false (old C-12).
- Every surviving item is tagged `Confirmed` (the claim holds) or `Corrected` (the claim held in part; the correction is stated in the item).
- Items that were wholly wrong were deleted. The old IDs of deleted, merged and renumbered items are in the appendix.
- Counting claims from the first draft (how many files, how many sessions) were not re-checked and are not used as evidence.
- Paths are relative to `skills/sohrab/` unless they start with `scripts/`, `README` or `artifacts/`. A reference cited by its numeric prefix alone is the file in that skill's `references/` directory that starts with that prefix.
- Line numbers are the numbers observed on 2026-10-18. Lines drift; locate a passage by its text.
- No repository checker covers any item here. `scripts/check_fleet_references.py` excludes line numbers by design, so a wrong line citation (A32) passes every gate.
- Coverage: the lanes read the cited files and their neighbours, not every reference of every skill. Absence of a finding elsewhere is unknown, not clean.
- Each item ends with a `sonnet Recommendation` box. The box states my own recommendation. Where it differs from the first draft or from the lane's proposal, it says why.
- Ownership follows `skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md` ("a rule has exactly one owning file"; "state every instruction exactly once"; "growth needs a reason").
- Items that need a decision from you (an owner choice, or a fact outside this repository) carry `Decision needed`.

## A. Contradictions

### A1. Arvan routing trigger has two forms
Severity: high. Status: Confirmed.
- Side 1: `README.fa.md:32` and `README.md:37` load `caas-arvan-kuber` whenever the work targets ArvanCloud CaaS ("Arvan-first wins").
- Side 2: `caas-arvan-kuber/SKILL.md:10-12` says being on Arvan is not by itself a reason to load the skill. It loads only when a fact is true of Arvan and false of stock Kubernetes.
- Sibling tables: `alaa-haproxy/references/90-companion-boundary.md:29` says "whenever the target is Arvan CaaS". `alaa-docker-production/references/90-companion-boundary.md:30` is a third form ("target runtime is Arvan CaaS rather than Compose or Swarm"). `alaa-k8s-helm/SKILL.md:19` and `references/openshift-and-managed-platforms.md:58` keep the generic skill for Arvan clusters. `alaa-k8s-helm/references/00-topic-map.md:67` and `version-awareness.md:41` carry the narrow test. `alaa-gitlab-ci-cd/references/90-companion-boundary.md:39` is neutral.
- Why it matters: the same Arvan Helm task routes differently depending on which file the agent reads first.
- Evidence added: the "Arvan-first wins" clause presumes the Arvan-fact test already passed. It is a precedence rule, not a load rule.
- Owner: the deciding test in `caas-arvan-kuber/SKILL.md:10`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep the narrow test in `caas-arvan-kuber/SKILL.md:10` as the only load rule and replace the other five trigger sentences (both READMEs, haproxy and docker boundary rows) with a pointer to it. Keep "Arvan wins" only as a precedence statement that applies after the skill has loaded. Decision needed: your global routing rule says Arvan CaaS overrides generic platform advice. That fits the precedence reading but not the broad load reading, so confirm that you want the narrow load test.

### A2. Ansible delivery gate is listed three ways
Severity: high. Status: Confirmed.
- `ansible-generator/SKILL.md:42-46` lists four commands: `check_templates.py`, `validate_*`, `scan_secrets.sh`, `check_task_safety.py`. No module-currency check.
- `ansible-generator/references/playbook.md` section 6 (about lines 226-254) lists five, including `check_module_currency.py`. Its accept condition is exit 0 from every command.
- `ansible-generator/references/best-practices.md` A13 (about 232-243) repeats the four-command form.
- Evidence added: `playbook.md:264` (the section 7 delivery block) also omits the currency check, so `playbook.md` disagrees with itself. `SKILL.md:19` and `best-practices.md:98` tell the agent to run the currency script, but no gate lists it. `scaffold.md:143` runs it for templates. The `ansible-validator` scripts do not call it.
- Why it matters: an agent following the SKILL gate skips the currency check and passes a module name that resolves only through a redirect.
- Owner: `playbook.md` section 6.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Make `playbook.md` section 6 the single gate list. Point `SKILL.md`, best-practices A13 and the section 7 "Checks:" line at it. A stronger alternative: have `ansible-validator`'s `validate_playbook.sh` call `check_module_currency.py`, so the four-command gate becomes complete by construction and no list can drift.

### A3. Laravel upgrade sweep: step 3 cannot apply the set that step 2 defines
Severity: high. Status: Corrected.
- `alaa-laravel-upgrade-all-packages/SKILL.md:23` says `--with-all-dependencies` "applies whatever the declared constraints permit, including a major bump" and tells the agent to split each major into its own change.
- `SKILL.md:24` then applies "the remaining set" with the same flag.
- Correction: "remaining set" is defined. `references/20-breaking-change-detection.md:43-49` defines the batch as patch, minor and transitive changes, and says majors leave the sweep. The defect is narrower: step 3 reuses the step 2 command, which cannot exclude a major under a loose constraint.
- Evidence added: `references/40-failure-classes.md:59,69` repeat the same command. `references/30-advisory-triage.md:22` and `20:49` use per-package `composer update <pkg> --with-dependencies`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep the procedure. Rewrite step 3 so that it applies only the packages classified patch or minor in the step 2 dry run, using per-package updates, and then check that the lock diff contains no major bump. The dry-run output is already the allow-list, so no new definition is needed. This also removes the redo risk in `02-optimization.md` O11.

### A4. Nobody owns a Laravel major-framework migration
Severity: medium. Status: Corrected. Decision needed.
- `alaa-php-clean-code/SKILL.md:26` sends dependency bumps to `alaa-laravel-upgrade-all-packages`. `alaa-php-clean-code/references/laravel-best-practices.md:30` says the same.
- `alaa-laravel-architecture/references/source-map.md:25` says the 12 to 13 dependency bumps are held in `alaa-php-clean-code references/laravel-best-practices.md`. This is the stale side.
- `alaa-laravel-upgrade-all-packages/SKILL.md:3,47` routes "major framework migration" to `alaa-laravel-architecture`, but architecture holds no migration content (it mentions "upgrade" only in `source-map.md` and `00-topic-map.md:16`).
- Correction: the first draft named the upgrade skill as owner. That is wrong as stated, because the upgrade skill excludes major framework migration in its own scope. The real defect is a routing cycle that ends at no content.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Fix `source-map.md:25` at once, since it is plainly stale. Then choose one: (a) declare in `SKILL.md:3,47` that the upgrade skill stops at dependency resolution and isolation (it already does this at `20:49`) and that code migration has no pack owner; or (b) give `alaa-laravel-architecture` a migration section. I recommend (a) now. Option (b) adds a capability and needs a real task to justify it under "growth needs a reason".

### A5. Octane scope predicate exists in two forms
Severity: medium. Status: Confirmed.
- `alaa-php-clean-code/SKILL.md:28` treats Octane as in scope unless `composer.json` lacks `laravel/octane` and there is no `config/octane.php`.
- `alaa-octane-performance/SKILL.md:16-19` scopes by `config('octane.server')` being non-null, "not from the package list".
- Effect: a repository with `config/octane.php` and a null server is in scope under the first rule and out of scope under the second.
- Evidence added: a third copy sits in `alaa-laravel-upgrade-all-packages/references/50-runtime-verification.md:7`. The two sides answer slightly different questions (conservative default for writing code, versus the load trigger of the specialist skill), but `AGENTS.md` still forbids two copies of one predicate.
- Owner: `alaa-octane-performance/SKILL.md:16`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Octane-performance keeps the predicate. In `alaa-php-clean-code` replace the predicate with a pointer and keep only the consequence ("assume Octane-safe by default when the predicate holds"). Point the upgrade skill's `50-runtime-verification.md:7` at the same owner.

### A6. Convention sentences tell the agent to write the dual call form
Severity: medium. Status: Corrected.
- `skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md:58-60` requires one `/name` form and treats existing dual call sites as legacy that converts only when a file is edited for another reason.
- Sentences that instruct a new agent to write both forms: `alaa-php-clean-code/SKILL.md:10` ("both forms appear at every call site"), `alaa-go-chi-development/SKILL.md:13`, and worst `alaa-services-contract/SKILL.md:80-81` ("every skill named anywhere in this pack takes both forms; reference files write the `$` form").
- More convention sentences found: `alaa-laravel-architecture/SKILL.md:12`, `alaa-laravel-public-api-contract-pack/SKILL.md:159`, `alaa-postman-collections/SKILL.md:91`, `alaa-keyset-pagination/SKILL.md:10`, `alaa-algorithms-data-structures/SKILL.md:8`, `alaa-system-design/SKILL.md:12`.
- Corrections: `alaa-security-review/SKILL.md:10` writes `/name` and only notes that Codex uses `$name`, so it is not a defect. The `clickhouse-performance-schema-ops` hit is a legacy pair in a description, not a convention sentence. The bare `$service-runtime-kit-governance` in `alaa-codex-runtime-ops/SKILL.md:100` and `references/20-command-and-path-discipline.md:38` is confirmed. `AGENTS.md` has no exemption for a Codex-only skill.
- Owner: `skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md` and `alaa-prompting-guide references/06-invocation-and-composition.md`. No skill owns it.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Rewrite only the convention sentences listed above, as one small change, and leave call sites alone, exactly as `AGENTS.md:60` says. Start with `alaa-services-contract:80-81` because it states the opposite of the rule. Convert the two bare `$` call sites in `alaa-codex-runtime-ops` the next time that skill is edited.

### A7. Keyset and services-contract list different offset-exception conditions
Severity: high. Status: Corrected. Decision needed.
- `alaa-keyset-pagination/references/10-route-mode-and-sort-allowlist.md:15-23` lists five conditions. Condition 3 is "documentation records pagination: offset with a named operational requirement". The exact-total point is condition 5. There is no growth bound.
- `alaa-services-contract/references/25-end-to-end-flow-and-boundaries.md:341-355` lists five different conditions, including "the list's size does not grow with tenant data", a documented maximum page size and a `400 INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED` reject (no clamp).
- Correction: the first draft misdescribed keyset condition 3. The two lists differ in both directions.
- Evidence added: ownership is circular. `25:365-366` says the five conditions "are owned by `/alaa-keyset-pagination`" and that this section is the contract text that authorizes them. Keyset `10:15` still says the contract "currently forbids" offset, which is stale. `alaa-laravel-public-api-contract-pack/references/30-pagination-and-limits-for-consumers.md:9-12` and `alaa-services-contract/references/40-apply-checklist-and-anti-patterns.md:115,220` cite the services-contract version. `CONTRACT-DECISIONS.md:58` proposes the growth-bound form.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep one list, in `alaa-services-contract` `25:341-355`, because that section is the text that authorizes the exception and keyset `10:15` explicitly waits for it. Merge the missing conditions (exact total bounded and measured) into it, delete the "owned by keyset" sentence at `25:365`, and make keyset `10` a pointer plus the algorithm rationale. Decision needed only if you want keyset to stay the owner of the list instead.

### A8. A request-time checker timeout maps to two status codes
Severity: high. Status: Confirmed. Decision needed.
- `alaa-trust-gateway-auth/SKILL.md:67` and `references/30-fail-closed-cases.md:57-64` deny a timed-out checker with `403 AUTHZ_DENIED`.
- `alaa-services-contract/references/26-request-time-authorization-openfga/40-decision-and-enforcement.md:9` lists `AUTHZ_SERVICE_TIMEOUT` and `AUTHZ_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as gateway-owned `503`. Files `10-model-and-tuple-flow.md:10` and `70-debugging-and-source-owners.md:27-28` in the same directory also treat timeout as fail-closed `503`.
- Nuance: the trust-gateway case also covers an unparseable answer, which the services-contract row does not.
- Owner: services-contract for the code row (`AGENTS.md`: wire shapes and codes).

> **sonnet Recommendation:** The pack cannot decide this from text: which status the gateway actually emits when the sidecar is silent is a fact about the gateway implementation, which is outside this repository. Decision needed: confirm the real behaviour. Then keep one row in services-contract `26/40`, let trust-gateway keep "deny, no service fallback" and cite the row, and correct whichever side is wrong. Do not edit either side before that confirmation.

### A9. Auth deny-code table: status mismatch and two duplicate rows
Severity: medium. Status: Corrected.
- `alaa-trust-gateway-auth/SKILL.md:66` and `references/30-fail-closed-cases.md:35` give a flat `401 AUTH_CONTEXT_MISSING`. `references/50-deny-codes.md:42` says "401 or 403 by service policy".
- Correction: the first draft said there are two owners and that the services-contract tree is missing the codes. That is mostly false. `alaa-services-contract/references/20-operational-and-observability-contract.md:174` says `AUTH_*` and `TENANT_CONTEXT_*` belong to trust-gateway `references/50-deny-codes.md`. The absence of these codes from services-contract is a delegation, not a gap.
- Real defects: (1) the 401 versus 401-or-403 mismatch above; (2) services-contract `26/40:7` also uses `401 AUTH_CONTEXT_MISSING` for the gateway path with a different meaning; (3) `AUTHZ_DENIED` is defined in both `50-deny-codes.md:52` and `26/40:6`, and `TOTP_STEP_UP_REQUIRED` in both `50:51` and a services-contract file.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Trust-gateway `50-deny-codes.md` owns the `AUTH_*`, `TENANT_CONTEXT_*` and `TOTP_*` rows, as services-contract already says. Align `SKILL.md:66` and case 1 to the table, and reduce the `AUTHZ_DENIED` row in `50` to a pointer to services-contract `26/40`. Add a one-line "code-registry owner" row to `AGENTS.md` only if you want the split recorded there.

### A10. Permission generator: unsourced frozen numbers
Severity: medium. Status: Corrected.
- `alaa-permission-generator/SKILL.md:69-70` states `MaxPermissionID()` values for three services (95, 119, 1). Lines 74-75 say no permission count or maximum id goes into code, a comment, a test or a report. Lines 78-83 give dated ranges ("still correct on 2026-07-27").
- Correction: the ban scopes to code, comments, tests and reports of a consuming service, not to this skill file, and the paragraph says "never from this paragraph", so it is not a literal self-contradiction.
- Real defect: the three values carry no source or date. `skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md` forbids a version-sensitive number without its source and date beside it. The numbers appear only in `SKILL.md`; `go-consumer.md:17` and `lifecycle.md:15` state the per-file rule without values.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Replace the three numbers with a generic illustration ("two services return different maxima"), since the rule is "per file, not per catalog" and needs no values. Move the dated ranges to a dated, sourced reference file or drop them.

### A11. Codex runtime ops records a "standing approval" with no provenance
Severity: medium. Status: Corrected. Decision needed.
- `alaa-codex-runtime-ops/references/40-project-fallbacks.md:5-7` says nine Quasar/Vite gates "have standing maintainer approval for unsandboxed execution when they are required validation gates, or when sandboxed esbuild `spawn EPERM` ... blocks completion". The file header calls it local operational fact.
- `alaa-codex-runtime-ops/SKILL.md:19` allows escalation only when the blocked command is necessary and its failure prevents completion. `references/20-command-and-path-discipline.md:77-79,88` keeps the per-command escalation path.
- Correction: the first draft said a skill cannot grant host permission and proposed deleting the section. The section records an approval; it does not grant one. The cited `SKILL.md:22` is only a pointer; the escalation rule is `SKILL.md:19`.
- Real defects: no approver, date or source is recorded, which fails the pack's "authoritative source for a concrete claim" rule; and the trigger "when they are required validation gates" (`:7`) drops the "failure prevents completion" condition of `SKILL.md:19`. The repository holds no grant record.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Do not delete the section. Add who approved it, when and where; state that it does not replace the harness prompt; and restrict it to "after the sandboxed run failed", as `SKILL.md:19` requires. Decision needed: only you can say whether you gave this approval. If you did not, replace the section with the command list as known candidates for the normal escalation path.

### A12. Service runtime kit governance commits by default
Severity: high. Status: Confirmed (re-read by the parent).
- `service-runtime-kit-governance/SKILL.md:55` step 5: "Commit the regenerated outputs."
- Root `AGENTS.md` and the global contract require explicit user authority before any commit. The skill and its references contain no commit-authorization wording; step 4 (secret check, "about to be committed") assumes the commit happens.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Replace step 5 with: leave the regenerated outputs uncommitted unless the user authorized a commit, and report the pending commit. Keep step 4 as a pre-commit check. No new owner is needed; commit authority already lives in `AGENTS.md`.

### A13. Memory OS: the store-neutral shape file requires vault fields
Severity: medium. Status: Confirmed (medium confidence on Hindsight mechanics).
- `alaa-memory-os/references/knowledge-shape.md:3` says it is store-agnostic, yet lines 13-24 require `permalink:` and `tags:` frontmatter and lines 29-32 a file-based checker. `references/prompt-3-publishing.md:42-46,79` publishes to vault paths and names `_global\lessons.md` warehouse paths (`:30-32`).
- `alaa-memory-os/SKILL.md:25-29` names such assumptions as policy leaks to repair. `SKILL.md:16` sets `ACTIVE_ADAPTER: hindsight`, so the leak is live.
- Evidence added: `references/store-local.md:71-77` already holds the vault frontmatter rule, so `knowledge-shape.md` duplicates it. `references/store-hindsight.md` (45 lines) maps no frontmatter, permalink or publication path. `knowledge-shape.md:115-119` correctly scopes Obsidian to file-backed stores. The cited lines 108-111 are the "adapter serialization" paragraph, which weakens the claim a little but does not close the gap.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep only neutral semantic fields in `knowledge-shape.md` (source paths, verified date, status, confidence). Move `permalink`, `tags` and the lessons publication paths to `store-local.md`, and add a Hindsight mapping to `store-hindsight.md`. Do not touch the legacy vault notes.

### A14. Go: "documented fire-and-forget" versus principle P9
Severity: medium. Status: Corrected.
- `alaa-golang/references/11-orchestration-and-overlap-guide.md:115-119` says it restates P9 and "does not soften it", yet allows a goroutine that is "a documented fire-and-forget whose failure is recorded as a metric".
- `alaa-golang-clean-code-principles/SKILL.md:89` and `references/30-runtime-and-observability.md:8-9` require an owner, a cancellation, a drain and a metric name.
- Correction: the conflict is smaller than the first draft said. File 11 (`:117-118`) still requires a component that stops the goroutine and a shutdown-cancelled context, so it is not ownerless. It omits the drain and the pooled-worker construct, and P9's three-condition data-loss exception (`30:39-44`) is not reachable through "documented". The phrase "fire-and-forget" occurs only at file 11:118.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Delete the "or is a documented fire-and-forget" clause in file 11 and point to P9 and its accepted-data-loss conditions. P9 in `alaa-golang-clean-code-principles` stays the owner.

### A15. Go: `WithoutCancel` drain example has no timeout
Severity: medium. Status: Confirmed.
- `alaa-golang-clean-code-principles/references/30-runtime-and-observability.md:25` shows `w.flush(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))` under "RIGHT".
- `alaa-golang/references/45-failure-behavior-at-the-call-site.md:252-253` forbids `WithoutCancel` without a following `WithTimeout`; the compliant form is at `:241`.
- Evidence added: the example might bound the timeout inside `flush`, which is not shown, so it is at best silent. `alaa-data-layer` `references/30-concurrency-projections-and-pooling.md:151` and `60-configuration-and-kit-gaps.md:103` document an unbounded `WithoutCancel` in a kit transaction rollback as a known kit gap, not as a skill example.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Change the clean-code example to `context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), budget)` with a one-line pointer to `alaa-golang` reference 45, the owner of the `WithoutCancel` rule.

### A16. Go: signal handling is both required and forbidden in one file
Severity: medium. Status: Confirmed.
- `alaa-golang/references/45-failure-behavior-at-the-call-site.md:210-219` says "create the process context with `signal.NotifyContext`".
- The same file, `:227-230`, forbids a service on the kit from implementing its own shutdown sequencing or signal handling.
- Evidence added: section 7 (`:205`) has no kit or standalone scope on its first rule, although section 5 (`:260`) uses "(kit)/(standalone)" labels. `alaa-golang/references/70-modern-go-baseline/30-runtime-and-standard-library.md:27` repeats the `NotifyContext` advice, also unscoped.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Scope `45:210-223` to "standalone service (no runkit)" and keep `:225-230` as the kit rule. Add the same scope to the `70-modern-go-baseline` line. Lifecycle ownership for the kit stays with `alaa-go-chi-development`.

### A17. Go: the `-race` and whole-suite gate is stated in four places
Severity: medium. Status: Confirmed.
- `alaa-golang/SKILL.md:66-72` assigns the whole-suite run to an authority other than the authoring lane and lists `-race` triggers (goroutine, channel, mutex, cache, worker pool, package-level variable).

# Skill pack review 02: optimization

Scope: the 69 skills under `skills/sohrab/`. Review date: 2026-10-18. This is the verified and corrected edition of the first draft.
Companion files: `01-contradictions-and-overlaps.md`, `03-new-skill-proposals.md`. Per-lane verdict notes: `verification/`.

## Purpose and method

This file lists skill content that makes an agent do unnecessary work or repeat work in the develop, debug and publish loop. It does not list style. Each item states the cost, where it sits, and the change that removes it.

- Every item was re-checked by a read-only lane (Sonnet 5.5) against the current source. The parent re-read the sources behind O7 and behind the file 01 items it cross-references that it verified itself (A11, A12, A33, A34, A43). Items are tagged `Confirmed` or `Corrected`.
- A first-draft item that was wholly style or weak (old O-04) was deleted. Items that only restate a defect already listed in file 01 are kept short here and cross-reference it, because their value in this file is the cost claim, and that claim was checked separately. Where the cost claim did not hold, the item says so.
- Body size is paid on every load of a skill; a reference is paid only when read (`skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md`, "Structure").
- Paths are relative to `skills/sohrab/` unless they start with `scripts/`.
- Every item ends with a `sonnet Recommendation` box. Where it differs from the first draft, it says why.
- The old-ID mapping is in the appendix.

## P. Priority finding: review, test and proof cadence

This section was added after the first edition of this review, on your request. The topic was absent from all three first-edition files: it was not in the first draft, and the first edition only touched it indirectly (O20 on the gate-economics wording, file 03 N6 on deploy-gate re-runs). It is placed first because repeated reviews, tests and proof tools are, by your assessment, one of the largest causes of slow runs.

Sources checked on 2026-10-18: `alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:96-110` and `:51-67`, `references/90-test-economy.md`; `alaa-cc-orchestrator/SKILL.md:87-110` and `references/verification-and-gates.md` (the codex twin differs only in runtime wording); `alaa-workflow/SKILL.md`, `references/task-tracking.md`, `references/workspace-and-integration.md`, `references/artifact-lifecycle.md`, `assets/plan-template.md`; and, outside the pack, the deploy repository's `AGENTS.md`. The installed copy of `alaa-workflow` and the repository copy were compared and are identical for the files cited.

The agent report you pasted cites four places. Re-reading them: `alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:104-106` (tier table), `verification-and-gates.md:66` (lane runs topic selectors) and `:27-30` (gate economics) are accurate. The deploy `AGENTS.md:141` is accurate too (a change under `tests/` other than `tests/runner/` is gated by the full strict gate). The agent's own conclusion also holds: the anti-repetition rule exists, but nothing forces it to be applied at the moment the agent decides to add a check.

### P1. The pack has no single end-to-end cadence, and its pieces do not match your rule
Status: Confirmed. Priority: high.

| Level | What the pack requires today | Matches your rule? |
|---|---|---|
| Subtask (a lane's unit of work) | The lane runs the focused tier at its end: topic selectors of its own failure-mode tests plus lint, type and build scoped to touched files (`alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:104`, `verification-and-gates.md:66`). | Yes, if the run stays short. The pack puts no size bound on a focused run (see P6). |
| Subtask review | Both orchestrators say Phase B ends with "a reviewable diff per completed subtask" (`SKILL.md:94`, codex `:90`) and the final success criteria say "every changed subtask has a reviewed diff and evidence" (`verification-and-gates.md:150`). | No. This asks for a reviewed diff per subtask. See file 01 A49. |
| Task (a tracked issue) | No separate level. `alaa-workflow/references/task-tracking.md:73` requires a close reason with "the reviewed version" for each task, which can be read as a per-task review. | Unclear. See P4 and file 01 A49. |
| Phase | The affected tier by an authority other than the author, once per phase (`alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:105`, Phase C), then the independent review of the complete diff (Phase D). | Yes for review at phase end. |
| Whole work | The exhaustive tier once, fresh, on the final candidate (`alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:106`, Phase E step 4), and the review. | Yes. |

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep the tier structure; it already agrees with your rule except at the subtask-review wording and the unbounded focused tier. State the cadence once, as a five-row table with your four levels, in `alaa-cc-orchestrator/references/verification-and-gates.md` and its codex twin in the same change (the mirrored pair), and have `alaa-testing-strategy` and `alaa-workflow` point to it instead of restating. The one rule that must read as a prohibition: no independent review and no independent verification at subtask or task end; review only at phase end and at the end of the whole work. Decision needed: whether your "test at the end of each task, without a review after it" means the existing focused tier (my reading) or the affected tier. The affected tier at every task end would add a run the pack does not require today.

### P2. Nothing makes an agent justify an added test, review, proof tool or gate
Status: Confirmed. Priority: high.
- What exists: `alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:40-47` ("a test is owed only for a decision this project makes, against a failure that can reach it") and `references/90-test-economy.md:63` (review check 1) cover new tests only. `verification-and-gates.md:73` requires a re-run to name "the changed condition or missing independent authority". `:27` requires a check list in the plan and says phase transitions and new agents earn no rerun.
- What does not exist: any admission test for a review lane beyond its trigger list, for an ad hoc proof tool (the pasted report describes a render counter plus a separate check of that counter), for a separately timed run, or for a self-test of a checker written in the same task. `:27` limits checker self-tests to the case where checker logic changes, but does not stop an agent from creating the checker.
- Why this is the leverage point: the agent in the pasted report knew the rule (`:27-30`) and still scheduled selected tests, a counting tool, a check of that tool, the full gate and a timed run. A rule that sits in prose is not applied; a field that must be filled at plan time is. `verification-and-gates.md:27` already requires one check list in the plan.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Add your rule as one sentence of binding text and one required column, and nothing else. Text, owner `alaa-testing-strategy` (it already owns "whether a test is owed"; put it beside that rule and widen the scope from "test" to "test, review, specialist, proof tool or gate"): "Before adding any test, review, proof tool or gate beyond the cadence default, state the real uncovered risk it checks and why existing evidence is insufficient; with no concrete answer, do not add it." Column: in the check list that `verification-and-gates.md:27` already requires, add "uncovered risk and why existing evidence is insufficient" for every entry that is not a cadence default. In `alaa-workflow/assets/plan-template.md` the phase field "Risk and required observers" is the plan-time home: change its prompt to ask the same question for every added check. Two pointers, no second statement. A cap on the number of cycles does not fix the cause, as the report says, so do not add one.

### P3. Review cadence: where each rule belongs, at plan time and at run time
Status: Corrected framing of your question. Priority: high.
- Plan time belongs to `alaa-workflow`: the plan records ordered phases, phase acceptance, "Risk and required observers" and validation commands (`assets/plan-template.md`, `references/artifact-lifecycle.md:11,30`). It is where the cadence and the P2 answers must be written before execution.
- Run time belongs to the orchestrator: it schedules lanes, verification and reviews (`verification-and-gates.md`, Phases B to E) and has the gate-economics rules.
- Test necessity and proof strength belong to `alaa-testing-strategy` (`SKILL.md:40-47`, tier table at `:96-110`).
- One more path: workflow can invoke the orchestrator once per phase (`alaa-workflow/SKILL.md`, "Delegate selectively"), which is where the next two items arise.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Both skills, one statement each, never the same sentence twice (`AGENTS.md`: state every instruction exactly once). (1) Orchestrator pair, in `verification-and-gates.md`: the cadence table and the "no review before phase end" prohibition. (2) `alaa-testing-strategy`: the admission sentence of P2. (3) `alaa-workflow`: one line in "Execute and resume" saying that the plan records the cadence per phase and that each added check carries its P2 answer, plus the plan-template prompt. The orchestrator and workflow cite the testing-strategy sentence by pointer.

### P4. The same selectors can run up to three times on an unchanged tree
Status: Confirmed. Priority: high. Cross-reference: file 01 A50.
- By design the author runs the focused selectors, an independent authority runs the affected tier (which is the union of selectors of every reachable topic and so includes the focused ones), and an independent authority runs the exhaustive tier (which includes everything). Reuse needs the "correct observer" (`verification-and-gates.md:110`), and the author is not an independent observer, so an author's focused result cannot be cited for the independent run. `alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:64` (non-negotiable 12) says breadth is earned by a change in the tree, and `:27` allows an aggregate to replace its identical children, but only when "required independent authority match". Neither says that the affected run is subsumed by an exhaustive run on the same tree.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Add one sentence to the cadence table of P1: when the exhaustive tier is required and runs on a tree that differs from the phase tree only by documentation, the exhaustive run discharges the affected tier and the affected run is not dispatched. Keep the author's focused run (it is cheap, fast feedback). This is the concrete form of the agent's first root cause, "when does an independent final run cover overlapping checks".

### P5. Workflow can invoke the orchestrator per phase, and each invocation reaches Phase E
Status: Confirmed. Priority: high. Cross-reference: file 01 A51.
- `alaa-workflow/SKILL.md` ("Delegate selectively") lets a phase run through the orchestrator. The orchestrator pipeline always reaches Phase E, whose step 4 runs "any required exhaustive tier once, fresh on the final candidate after documentation". For a workflow of several phases nothing says that "final candidate" means the last phase.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** In the cadence table add: an orchestrator run that executes a non-final workflow phase stops at Phase D (affected tier plus the one review); the exhaustive tier and the documentation gate belong to the last phase. State it in `verification-and-gates.md` and have `alaa-workflow` point to it.

### P6. The focused tier has no stated bound
Status: Confirmed. Priority: medium.
- `alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:104` and `verification-and-gates.md:66` require a focused run per subtask and say "scoped" and "topic selectors", but nothing says what makes a run too big to be focused. Your exception (a very short test of the same subtask) fits only if the focused tier is short.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Define focused by what it needs, not by a duration the pack cannot source: a focused run uses only the subtask's own topic selectors and scoped lint, type and build; a run that needs a container, a service, the full gate or more than the touched topic is not focused and moves to the phase level. This keeps your exception testable without hard-coding a number.

### P7. A repository gate scope can override the pack
Status: Confirmed (source outside the pack). Priority: high for that repository.
- `deploy/AGENTS.md:141` makes `scripts/chart-gate.sh --strict` the gate for any change under `tests/` other than `tests/runner/`, plus many other paths, and requires containers on a Windows host. `alaa-testing-strategy/SKILL.md:20` and `verification-and-gates.md:25` say a repository's own validation policy outranks the pack, so no pack text can narrow this.
- The pack already says how to avoid it: `alaa-testing-strategy/references/90-test-economy.md:27` says the repository records a selector map of topic, layer and exact command, and `alaa-project-constitution` carries the slot.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Fix it in the deploy repository, not in the pack: map changed paths to gates, run the strict gate for a delivery handoff or a change to the chart, values or CI, and let a change to a single check under `tests/` run that check's own selector. Separately, check that `alaa-project-constitution` requires the validation policy to carry a changed-path to gate map as well as the selector map; I did not verify that file, so confirm before editing.

## A. Always-paid body size

### O1. The largest skill bodies
Status: Corrected.
- Cost: a body is read whenever the skill is triggered, even when the task needs one section.
- Measured on 2026-10-18 (bytes of `SKILL.md` / lines): `alaa-testing-strategy` 30726/208; `alaa-php-clean-code` 25808/209; `alaa-system-design` 19422/169; `alaa-algorithms-data-structures` 19058/156; `alaa-codex-orchestrator` 18356/172; `alaa-reliability-sla` 17856/143; `alaa-cc-orchestrator` 17686/171; `alaa-laravel-job-rabbitmq` 16328/209; `alaa-security-review` 15823/147; `alaa-keyset-pagination` 15276/95. Next: `alaa-project-constitution` 15022, `alaa-permission-generator` 14526, `alaa-memory-os` 14443.
- Correction: the first draft's table omitted `alaa-laravel-job-rabbitmq` and `alaa-keyset-pagination`, ranked `alaa-project-constitution` and `alaa-memory-os` as 9 and 10 when they are 11 and 13, and put the orchestrator pair in the wrong order. Its sizes for the listed skills were accurate.
- Evidence added: `python scripts\validate_sohrab_skill_pack.py` exits 0 and prints 21 body-length warnings. Rule V4 warns above 120 lines (`scripts/validate_sohrab_skill_pack.py:114`, `BODY_LINE_WARN = 120`). `AGENTS.md` states no numeric body limit. A body over the line threshold is a warning, not a defect. Bytes are the better signal: `alaa-keyset-pagination` has 95 lines and no warning but is the tenth largest body.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Treat size as a ranking tool, not a defect list. Start with `alaa-testing-strategy` and `alaa-php-clean-code`, and for each one move consulted material to `references/`, keeping role, trigger, procedure, stop conditions and one-line pointers. Do not shorten a body that carries a behaviour rule. Change nothing in a skill just to clear the warning. Because the doctrine added today (`4d5f295aa`) lives in a reference, the testing-strategy body may already be close to its target; measure again after any change.

### O2. Duplicated routers in always-paid bodies
Status: Corrected. Cross-reference: file 01 B13, B14.
- Cost: a router in the body costs tokens on every load and drifts. `AGENTS.md` states the rule: one router per skill; with 9 or more references the router moves to `references/00-topic-map.md` and the body keeps exactly one pointer line.
- Where: `alaa-frontend-developer/SKILL.md:69-85` ("Also load" table with different triggers; its own line 67 says "do not route from this file"); `alaa-quasar-app-vite-v3/SKILL.md:38-47` ("Mandatory pairings" bullets); `alaa-reliability-sla/SKILL.md:107-119` (bullet list of 8 references beside a topic map); `alaa-services-contract/SKILL.md:53-73` (a true duplicate that has drifted: no rows for 05 or 29).
- Correction: the four bodies differ in kind, and reliability-sla's count is ambiguous (8 content references plus the map).

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Do the services-contract change first, since it has already drifted. For reliability-sla settle the counting rule before touching anything. In the other two, fold the rows into the topic map and leave one pointer line. Keep any "blocking gate" sentence that is a rule, not a route.

### O3. A dated observation in the minio body, and an inconsistent source name
Status: Corrected.
- Where: `alaa-minio-object-storage/SKILL.md:71-82` ("What the fleet does today").
- Correction: the section is not "unverifiable". It carries a source and a read date (line 74) and says it is "never platform policy". The cost is small (12 lines).
- Real defect: the source name. The body says "tusd-upload-platform repository" (a skill name), while `tusd-upload-platform/SKILL.md:16` says "the Ala tusd repository". The phrase "tusd-upload-platform repository" recurs about 30 times in minio references.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Make the name consistent in minio `SKILL.md` and `references/SOURCES.md`. Moving the section to a reference is optional and worth doing only when the body is next edited.

## B. Mandatory scaffolds that apply to every change

### O4. Shaka Player forces parts of the pipeline on any change
Status: Corrected.
- Where: `alaa-shaka-player/SKILL.md:58-65` (six steps) and `:69`.
- Correction: the six steps are not all unconditional. Step 4 is "the capability the task actually asked for", and the output items are scoped to what changed ("error classes it newly handles", "quantities it emits"). Unconditional parts: step 2 (reading reference 80 and running `check-shaka-api.mjs`) and the QA evidence. A one-line config edit still pays for those.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Scope step 2 and the QA clause by change type: run the API check when the change adds or alters a `player.configure()` option or an error path, and ship QA evidence proportional to the change. Leave the other steps as they are.

### O5. Tusd returns ten items for every design or review
Status: Confirmed.
- Where: `tusd-upload-platform/SKILL.md:66`: "for design or review work, return" ten items (register, topology, authorization, size chain, retention, hook posture, lifecycle, observability, tests, risks), with no scope condition.
- Cost: a review of one hook returns the same ten items.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Add "for each item in scope" and list which items each change type needs (a hook review needs hook posture, lifecycle, observability and tests, for example). Keep the ten as the full-design set.

### O6. Frontend QA runs SSR and service-worker checks with no trigger
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 B12.
- Where: `alaa-frontend-developer/references/50-qa-and-verification.md:27` ("Mandatory SSR and hydration checks") and the service-worker runbook at `:33-47`. Quasar `75-testing-ci-playbook.md:22-31` already has an "Applies when" column (for example "the SSR mode exists"). The frontend file's line 66 says "proportional to the risk", which softens the effect slightly.
- Cost: a CSS-only change, or a repository with no PWA mode, is told to run both.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Add the same "applies when" column to both sections. This pairs with moving the runbook to Quasar `75` (file 01 B12), so the trigger lives in one place.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Same as file 01 A34: report the missing guard as a finding and install it only when the request names it or you approve.

Status: Corrected. Cross-reference: file 01 A17.

### O9. Go: the TDD sequence is repeated and shortened
Status: Corrected. Cross-reference: file 01 B16.
- Where: Fiber `30-validation-testing.md:117-121` (three steps) and `alaa-golang-clean-code-principles/references/40-testing-and-contracts.md:20` (one line, whose `:44` already points to the owner).

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Point the Fiber copy at reference 63 (file 01 B16). The clean-code one-liner already points there and can stay.

### O10. Auditing an OpenAPI or Postman contract re-derives the owner's rules
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 B5.

## C. Loop-level rework

### O11. Upgrade sweep with an unusable apply step
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 A3.

Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 A2.

Status: Corrected (low severity).

### O17. Docker version table is dated
Status: Corrected.
- Where: `alaa-docker-production/references/10-dockerfile-authorship.md:188-197`: "current as of 2026-07-29", with Node 24 "Active LTS to 2026-10-20, then maintenance to 2028-04-30".

The table label ("as of 2026-07-29") is older than the `check-image-pinning.mjs` rows (2026-09-29), and that script is the live source (`:126`). Line 188 already says to re-run `--versions`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Re-date the table from the script's output now (the script is the authority), and keep the instruction to re-run `--versions` before writing any default.

## D. Duplicated reading cost

These items are not wrong on their own. Each adds a file an agent reads to confirm a rule that another file states.

### O18. Keyset restates the envelope and the limits
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 B8.
- Where: `alaa-keyset-pagination/references/40-wire-contract-limits-and-errors.md:9-36`, which says it states "only what keyset adds"; `SKILL.md:56-58` repeats it.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep only the algorithm rationale and link to services-contract `25` for the envelope; fix the false limit claim at keyset `SKILL.md:50` first (file 01 B8).

### O19. Fiber restates many owners
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 B17, B18, B19.
- Where: `alaa-golang-fiber/references/40-production-readiness.md:36-38,46-64,81-88,94-103`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** A pointer per rule, as in file 01 B17 to B19. The shedding pointer to `alaa-reliability-sla` is missing and is the first one to add.

### O20. The gate-economics rule appears in three independent files
Status: Corrected. Cross-reference: file 01 B28.
- Correction: the rule text is in `alaa-cc-orchestrator/SKILL.md:63` (and its allowed mirror), `alaa-prompting-guide/SKILL.md:65` and `alaa-low-noise/references/model-output-profiles.md:16-18`. `alaa-workflow/SKILL.md:43` states a different rule. The first draft counted five copies. Token cost is trivial; drift risk is real.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Low priority. Move the rule into the orchestrators' `verification-and-gates.md` and point the other two at it when next touched.

### O21. Dispatch return contract across several owners
Status: Corrected. Cross-reference: file 01 B26.
- Correction: `alaa-workflow/SKILL.md:63` is a pointer, not an owner. The clauses are in low-noise, workflow `context-continuity.md:132` and the orchestrators' `delegation-prompts.md`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** One owner for the bound and rationale (`alaa-low-noise/references/workflow-integration.md`), with the orchestrators keeping the `<return>` field plus a pointer.

### O22. ClickHouse boundary and worked instance
Status: Corrected (low severity). Cross-reference: file 01 B25.
- Where: `clickhouse-performance-schema-ops/references/15-fleet-clickhouse-boundary.md:83-110` embeds a commit hash and line numbers. The section says to re-derive the commit before repeating it and lives in a reference, so it is read on demand. The boundary text in the two `SKILL.md` files is two or three lines each.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Replace the hash and line numbers with a named placeholder and keep the boundary in one place. Optional beyond that.

### O23. Bale and Mediana restate reliability and security rules
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 B21, B22.
- Where: `alaa-bale-provider/SKILL.md:79` (`98912****000`) and `alaa-sms-provider-mediana/SKILL.md:62` (`+9891****0000`) differ; both restate the five-egress rule and the connect-refused versus timeout split.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Keep only the vendor-specific column in each provider and point to the owning security and reliability references (file 01 A42, B21, B22).

## E. Maintenance-driven rework

### O24. Dated facts without a refresh trigger
Status: Corrected (low severity).
- Where: `alaa-golang-fiber/SKILL.md:19-28`, `alaa-golang-clean-code-principles/references/30-runtime-and-observability.md:101-105`, `alaa-golang-fiber/references/40-production-readiness.md:69-76`, `50:41-47`.
- Correction: all four sites carry a source and a date, which `AGENTS.md` asks for. What is missing is a re-check trigger. This is mostly a style gap.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Add one re-check trigger per section ("re-verify before changing a Fiber default"). Do not rewrite the facts.

### O25. A date inside a durable rule
Status: Confirmed.
- Where: `alaa-mongodb-patterns/SKILL.md:14-15`: "On 2026-07-26 no service in `alaa-go-chi docs/CONSUMERS.md` runs MongoDB". The sentence is a rationale inside a "when not to use" rule. The source file is in another repository and cannot be verified here.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** State the rule without the date and keep the source as a pointer with a re-check trigger. A rule that depends on an external repository's state should say how to re-check it.

### O26. Phase gate duplicated with its dated facts
Status: Confirmed. Cross-reference: file 01 A18.
- Where: `alaa-golang-clean-code-principles/SKILL.md:26-37`, `references/90-source-map.md:48`, and the routing sentence at `alaa-golang/references/00-topic-map.md:82`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Delete the restated gate and point to `alaa-go-chi-development` reference 05 and `scripts/phase-check.sh` (file 01 A18).

### O27. Shaka and indexeddb carry the same block
Status: Corrected. Cross-reference: file 01 B23.

- A cleanup nit, not an agent cost: `alaa-shaka-player/assets/templates/offlineDownload.ts` is referenced by no file in the skill (the filename appears nowhere in the skill directory, re-grepped). It belongs in a separate tidy-up change; check first whether the other templates are listed in a topic map.

# Skill pack review 03: new skill proposals from chat evidence

Scope: local agent transcripts from the window 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-18, read by the first-draft agent to find repeated work, repeated errors and learning cost. This is the verified and corrected edition.
Companion files: `01-contradictions-and-overlaps.md`, `02-optimization.md`. Per-lane verdict notes: `verification/`.

## Sources, limits and how this edition was checked

- The first draft mined Claude Code transcripts (four projects: `alaa-go-chi`, `client`, `deploy`, `skills`) and Codex sessions. ChatGPT web chats are not available locally, so that side of the evidence is absent.
- Codex inter-agent message bodies are encrypted, so orchestrator-to-subagent corrections cannot be seen. Some Claude sessions look like forks of each other, which can inflate any repeat claim.
- Instruction for this edition: transcript counts (sessions, error totals, costs, minutes) were not re-checked and are not used as evidence. Only the reasoning and the conclusions drawn from the pack's own references were judged. Where a conclusion rested only on a count, the item says so.
- Everything about what the pack covers was re-checked by a read-only lane (Sonnet 5.5) and, for the key items, by the parent. Items are tagged `Confirmed` or `Corrected`.
- One first-draft item (old N-8, "no skill states commit-scope isolation") was wrong and was deleted. Its replacement fact is recorded in the verification table below.
- Paths are relative to `skills/sohrab/` unless stated. Every item ends with a `sonnet Recommendation` box.

## Verification table: coverage claims in the pack

| # | Claim in the first draft | Result | Corrected fact |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | Sentry appears in only a few skill files | Corrected | Sentry appears in many files. The substantive content is in `alaa-observability-soc/references/60-sentry-and-profiling.md`, `alaa-vue-typescript-clean-code/references/74-observability-binding.md:73-78` (one facade) and a tusd asset `quasar.boot.sentry.ts` (before-send scrub). `alaa-quasar-app-vite-v3/references/36-client-observability-contract.md` uses Sentry only as a scrub example. |
| V2 | Browser or Quasar Sentry SDK setup is not covered | Corrected | Partial gap, with a sharper cause: `60-sentry-and-profiling.md:5` says env variable names belong to `alaa-services-contract`, but `alaa-services-contract/references/21-alaa-platform-observability-directive.md` holds no Sentry env names, package set or DSN. The pointer dangles. `60:50,58` cover DSN-not-committed, release injection and CI tokens, all server-side. Browser DSN and SSR wiring are absent. |
| V3 | Git Bash "signal pipe" is covered | Confirmed | `alaa-codex-runtime-ops/SKILL.md:51` and `references/20-command-and-path-discipline.md:48`. |
| V4 | PowerShell `InitializeDefaultDrives` warning has no coverage | Confirmed | Zero hits in the pack. It is a profile warning, not a command failure; whether it breaks any command is unproven. |
| V5 | `apply_patch` failures have no coverage | Confirmed | The only hit is `alaa-prompting-guide/references/10-gpt-5-6.md:60`, an API tool-type list, not Codex CLI patch guidance. |
| V6 | No skill covers Stop-hook or `/goal` conditions | Corrected | `alaa-prompting-guide/references/41-claude-code-runtime-features.md:131-135` covers the Claude evaluator. Line 133 says evaluator verdicts are not evidence that repository gates passed; line 135 says Codex `/goal` is not a Stop-hook evaluator. `references/06-invocation-and-composition.md:45-62` and `scripts/check_goal_condition.py` cover composition. |
| V7 | No skill covers a GitLab runner Compose bootstrap | Confirmed | `alaa-gitlab-ci-cd` mentions Compose only in `references/container-build-strategies.md:5` and `references/90-companion-boundary.md:37`, which hands Compose authorship to `alaa-docker-production` (`references/20-compose-authorship.md` covers Compose generally). |
| V8 | Commit `4d5f295aa` (test-economy doctrine) exists | Confirmed | The doctrine is `alaa-testing-strategy/references/90-test-economy.md`. It covers test design and sharing, not deploy-gate selection. |
| V9 | The Persian-language rule belongs to a skill | Corrected | Persian is mentioned in dozens of pack files (mostly ui-ux, repo-docs, input-normalization). The user-language rule is not in the pack; `skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md` says the reply language is the user's. A skill is the wrong place. |

## Recommendation summary

Most chat evidence is either covered by an existing owner or belongs to a tool or harness rather than a skill. No new skill is justified now.

| # | Topic | Type | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | GitLab runner Compose bootstrap | learning cost | No new skill. If it recurs, extend `alaa-gitlab-ci-cd` |
| N2 | Browser Sentry SDK wiring for Quasar SPA and SSR | repeated derivation | Fix the dangling name pointer first, then extend `alaa-quasar-app-vite-v3`. No new skill |
| N3 | Codex patch failures and exec-wrapper syntax | repeated error | Not in `alaa-codex-runtime-ops`, except one clause. Owner decision needed |
| N4 | Windows shell and process failures (Codex) | repeated error | Do not extend until the exact failing text is known |
| N5 | Premature completion against goal and Stop-hook gates | repeated error | No change |
| N6 | Central-delivery gate re-runs and re-reads | repeated error | No skill. Fix the cadence rules in the pack first (file 02 section P), then the deploy gate scope |
| N7 | Subagent re-reads of global rules and skills | repeated derivation | No change until the cause is known |
| N8 | Persian-language drift | repeated error | No skill; outside the pack |

## N1. GitLab runner Compose bootstrap

Type: learning cost. Status: Corrected. Confidence in the pattern: low to medium (one long session).
- Evidence (reasoning only): one long session in the deploy project (the session file exists) worked through token entry, three TLS verify modes the user had to name in turn (`insecure`, `verified`, `unverified`), a `RUNNER_COMPOSE_DIR` that must hold no spaces, shell and PowerShell errors, and parity between the `.sh` and `.ps1` bootstrap scripts. Duration and cost figures were not re-checked and are not used.
- Coverage gap: confirmed (V7). `alaa-gitlab-ci-cd` covers `config.toml`, executors and pipeline authoring, not a Compose bootstrap.
- Correction: the first draft said a second occurrence is the bar for building a skill. `skills/sohrab/AGENTS.md` has no such bar; its relevant rules are "state every instruction exactly once", ownership, and "growth needs a reason". The "wait for a second occurrence" bar is the draft's own judgment.
- Boundary: runner `config.toml` stays with `alaa-gitlab-ci-cd`. Compose authorship stays with `alaa-docker-production` (`references/20-compose-authorship.md`).

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Do not create `alaa-gitlab-runner-compose-bootstrap`. A bootstrap script pair with path checks and a TLS mode is mostly deploy-repository content, and a single session is thin evidence. If the pattern recurs, add a short runner-Compose section to an `alaa-gitlab-ci-cd` runner reference (for example the shell and Kubernetes executor reference) that defers Compose authorship to `alaa-docker-production` reference 20 and records the TLS mode as a decision the user makes once. Keep the scripts themselves in the deploy repository.

## N2. Browser Sentry SDK wiring for Quasar SPA and SSR

Type: repeated derivation and learning cost. Status: Corrected. Confidence: medium. Decision needed.
- Evidence (reasoning only): three client sessions opened with the same question, whether Sentry is set up, and their Stop-hook conditions included a dev-test Sentry acceptance. The mention counts and any fork inflation were not re-checked.
- Coverage: partial (V1, V2). `alaa-observability-soc` `60-sentry-and-profiling.md` owns the role split and gates. Quasar `36-client-observability-contract.md` (56 lines) owns the scrub-before-transport rule at `:37` and already has a section "Wiring in a Quasar app" (`:46-51`).
- New finding: the names are blocked, not just missing. `60:5` sends env names to `alaa-services-contract`, which holds none for Sentry (V2), and Quasar `36:5` forbids inventing names. An agent cannot write a client SDK reference without inventing them.
- Placement rules: the Quasar skill has no free numbering problem (33 references, free slots 33, 38, 39), but a new file needs a `00-topic-map.md` row and a trigger-form body pointer (`AGENTS.md`, "Structure"). Public-DSN and SDK behaviour is a version-sensitive external fact.
- Owner boundary: event and env names stay with `alaa-services-contract`; gates stay with `alaa-observability-soc`.

> **sonnet Recommendation:** Do not add a new skill, and do not add a new reference file yet. First settle the owner of the client Sentry env and package names (a services-contract entry in reference 21, or an explicit statement that the client has none), because the current pointer dangles. Then extend section 5 of Quasar `36` with initialisation point, DSN as a public value, SSR versus client split and the env contract, since that section already holds wiring. Obtain the SDK facts from current official Sentry documentation through a research lane, and name the new capability in the change ("growth needs a reason"). Decision needed: who owns the client Sentry names.

## N3. Codex patch failures and exec-wrapper syntax

Type: repeated error then fix. Status: Corrected. Decision needed.
- Evidence (reasoning only): repeated `apply_patch verification failed` outputs, mostly "failed to find expected lines" and "multiple operations target", and syntax errors from the JavaScript exec wrapper when shell syntax was written into it. The counts were not re-checked.
- Coverage: none for patch failure (V5).
- Correction: the first draft said runtime failures are `alaa-codex-runtime-ops`' family. That is wrong for a patch context mismatch. The skill's description excludes application, test, migration and domain failures, and a stale-context patch is an agent tool-use error, not a harness failure.
